### <span class="imp imp-high" title="Importance 7/10" aria-label="Importance 7 of 10">7</span> SpaceX projects $500 billion revenue by 2028, expanding into AI
SpaceX projects $500 billion in revenue by 2028 as it pivots toward artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company plans to deploy 6–10 gigawatts of AI computing capacity by end of 2027, targeting $300 billion in annual recurring revenue with Microsoft reportedly negotiating a $150 billion deal.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>Projected $500 billion revenue by 2028</li>
<li>6–8 GW AI computing capacity by 2027; potential &gt;10 GW by year-end</li>
<li>$300 billion annual recurring revenue target from AI infrastructure</li>
<li>Microsoft in talks for reported $150 billion client deal</li>
</ul>

## Space Events

### <span class="imp imp-mid" title="Importance 6.5/10" aria-label="Importance 6.5 of 10">6.5</span> Total Solar Eclipse Crosses Greenland, Iceland, and Spain Today
A total solar eclipse crosses Greenland, Iceland, and Spain on August 12, 2026—Spain's first since 1905. About 230 million people will experience 90% totality or greater, with partial visibility across much of the Northern Hemisphere including major European cities and parts of North America.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>Path of totality reaches Iceland at 5:48 p.m. local time, Spain at 8:28–8:32 p.m.</li>
<li>Spain&#x27;s first total solar eclipse since 1905</li>
<li>~230 million people able to see ≥90% totality</li>
<li>Partial visibility in London, Paris, Madrid (90%+); Boston (16%); New York City (9%)</li>
<li>Only total solar eclipse of 2026</li>
</ul>

Sources: [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/total-solar-eclipse-august-12-2026/) <span class="src-badge src-research">AI Web Searched</span>, [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/graphics/SOLAR-ECLIPSE/MAPS/mopazzzxova/) <span class="src-badge src-research">AI Web Searched</span>, [Space.com](https://www.space.com/stargazing/solar-eclipses/a-total-solar-eclipse-will-darken-the-sky-for-millions-today-aug-12-2026-heres-what-you-need-to-know) <span class="src-badge src-rss">RSS</span>
